whyItMatters: The clearest evidence that a new role was built for operational abuse is that it gets assumed quickly after creation. This moves the signal from suspicious setup to confirmed activation.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may create a role, optionally grant it permissions, and then assume it shortly afterward to exercise the new trust path.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is one of the strongest role-based persistence patterns because it directly links provisioning to immediate use.
threatContext.whyItMatters: CreateRole alone is only setup. AssumeRole is the proof the new role became active infrastructure.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may see role creation as just another provisioning event while the attacker is already operating through the new role.

loggingRequirements: Both CreateRole and AssumeRole telemetry must be ingested.
Correlations should prefer exact role ARN or account-qualified role identity over role name only.
The environment should preserve trust and permission context from the newly created role.
limitations: Role-name-only matching can fail when paths are used or names repeat across accounts.
Some legitimate testing and CI/CD workflows create and assume roles quickly.
AssumeRole success is the key event, so failed assumptions should be analyzed separately.

rawToNormalized.notes: Role assumed by later STS call
Account boundary for exact role correlation
Actor creating or assuming the role

enrichment.description: Correlate the created role to later AssumeRole using ARN, account ID, and path-aware role identity.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Prevents false joins across reused names or path variations.

enrichment.description: Carry forward trust-policy and permission-risk classification from creation time.
Determine who assumed the role and whether that assumer was expected.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Distinguishes ordinary testing from suspicious activation patterns.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This should be the anchor high-confidence rule in the role-creation family. First observe a successful CreateRole, then correlate a later successful AssumeRole into that exact role within a short window, and enrich with trust, permissions, and assumer context.
conditions: second eventSource equals sts.amazonaws.com and eventName equals AssumeRole
requestParameters.roleArn resolves to the same role created earlier
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Correlate on exact role identity, not just role name. 2. Carry forward trust and permission risk from `det-061` and `det-062`. 3. Escalate for external-account assumption or same-session creator-to-assumer continuity.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when a newly created role is assumed shortly afterward, especially when the role had risky trust or high-risk permissions.

simulationCommand: aws iam create-role --role-name BackdoorRole --assume-role-policy-document file://trust-policy.json && aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/BackdoorRole --role-session-name backdoor-test

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium depending on legitimate create-and-test workflows

whereItRuns: Athena with exact role identity joins
deployment.scheduling: Best in near-real-time because role activation soon after creation is highly actionable.
considerations: This is one of the highest-fidelity role-abuse detections in the dataset.
